WI.mailModel: No-excuse absentee — voters may request an absentee ballot without an excuse. Some voters with disabilities may join a continuing absentee list. Some senior voters may join a continuing absentee list.
WI.notableRule: Some voters with disabilities and some seniors can join continuing absentee lists.
WI.featureTags: Open primary; No statewide RCV; No standard runoff; No-excuse absentee; Disability absentee list; Senior absentee list
WI.explainer: Wisconsin uses an open primary. Absentee voting is available without an excuse.

WY.primarySystem: Closed primary — voters generally participate only in their own party's primary.
WY.rankedChoiceStatus: RCV prohibited — ranked-choice voting is barred by state law.
WY.mailModel: No-excuse absentee — voters may request an absentee ballot without an excuse. Some small or local elections may be conducted by mail.
WY.featureTags: Closed primary; RCV prohibited; No standard runoff; No-excuse absentee; Small-election mail
WY.explainer: Wyoming uses a closed primary, so voters generally participate only in their own party’s primary. State law bars regular ranked-choice voting and absentee voting is available without an excuse.

DC.primarySystem: District primary rules — party primaries are administered under D.C. election law.
DC.rankedChoiceStatus: RCV required — primary, special and general elections for city and federal offices use ranked-choice voting.
DC.runoffRules: RCV replaces runoff — covered contests use ranked-choice voting instead of a separate runoff.
DC.mailModel: All-mail — every registered voter is mailed a ballot for every election.
DC.notableRule: D.C. pairs broad RCV coverage with universal mail ballots.
DC.featureTags: District; District primary rules; RCV required; RCV replaces runoff; All-mail; Permanent absentee list
DC.explainer: D.C. uses ranked-choice voting for city and federal primary, special and general elections, and it also mails every registered voter a ballot.

AS.primarySystem: Territorial election rules — the Senate is selected under Samoan custom.
AS.rankedChoiceStatus: No territory-wide RCV — no territorial ranked-choice voting rule is highlighted in the cited sources.
AS.mailModel: Territory rules — see the territorial election office for current absentee and mail-ballot procedures.
AS.notableRule: Territorial senators are selected by county councils under Samoan custom rather than by a standard statewide popular vote.
AS.featureTags: Territory-specific; Territory-specific senate selection; No territory-wide RCV; No standard runoff; Territory mail rules
AS.explainer: American Samoa is unusual because its Senate is chosen by county councils under Samoan custom instead of through the standard direct-election model used in states.

GU.primarySystem: Partisan primary — the ballot includes separate party columns and a non-affiliated column.
GU.rankedChoiceStatus: No territory-wide RCV — no territorial ranked-choice voting rule is highlighted in the cited sources.
GU.mailModel: Territory rules — see the territorial election office for current absentee and mail-ballot procedures.
GU.notableRule: Independent candidates face vote thresholds in the primary to reach the general election ballot.
GU.featureTags: Territory-specific; Territory-specific primary rules; No territory-wide RCV; No standard runoff; Territory mail rules
GU.explainer: Guam’s primary ballot separates party and non-affiliated columns, and voters can only choose one track. Independent candidates also have vote thresholds to reach the general election.

MP.primarySystem: Commonwealth election rules — territorial offices follow CNMI election law.
MP.rankedChoiceStatus: No territory-wide RCV — no territorial ranked-choice voting rule is highlighted in the cited sources.
MP.runoffRules: Territory runoff — governor/lieutenant governor and attorney general go to a runoff 14 days after certification if no one wins a majority.
MP.mailModel: Territory rules — see the territorial election office for current absentee and mail-ballot procedures.
MP.notableRule: Governor/lieutenant governor and attorney general races can trigger a runoff 14 days after certification.
MP.featureTags: Territory-specific; Territory election rules; No territory-wide RCV; Territory runoff; Territory mail rules
MP.explainer: In the Northern Mariana Islands, governor/lieutenant governor and attorney general candidates must win a majority or go to a runoff 14 days after certification.

PR.primarySystem: Party primaries — territorial parties may hold primaries, and presidential primaries may also be scheduled.
PR.rankedChoiceStatus: No territory-wide RCV — no territorial ranked-choice voting rule is highlighted in the cited sources.
PR.mailModel: Territory rules — see the territorial election office for current absentee and mail-ballot procedures.
PR.notableRule: The election commission also runs presidential primaries and status plebiscites when scheduled.
PR.featureTags: Territory-specific; Territory party primaries; No territory-wide RCV; No standard runoff; Territory mail rules
PR.explainer: Puerto Rico’s election commission runs general elections, local primaries and other electoral events, including presidential primaries and status plebiscites when scheduled.

VI.primarySystem: Territorial election rules — executive races can require a majority runoff.
VI.rankedChoiceStatus: No territory-wide RCV — no territorial ranked-choice voting rule is highlighted in the cited sources.
VI.runoffRules: Territory runoff — the governor/lieutenant governor ticket must win a majority or face a runoff 14 days later.
VI.mailModel: Territory rules — see the territorial election office for current absentee and mail-ballot procedures.
VI.notableRule: Governor and lieutenant governor run as one ticket and must win a majority or go to a runoff.
VI.featureTags: Territory-specific; Territory election rules; No territory-wide RCV; Territory runoff; Territory mail rules
VI.explainer: In the U.S. Virgin Islands, governor and lieutenant governor run as one ticket and must win a majority; otherwise the top two go to a runoff two weeks later.
